title: Peasant thumb mittens
subtitle: Full mittens with a peasant thumb, worked in the round in DK wool.
excerpt: Full mittens in DK wool with a peasant thumb, worked in the round. The peasant thumb is the simplest thumb opening: a single row of waste yarn marks the position, and the thumb is worked from the live stitches after the hand is complete. Sized for hand circumferences of 18, 20, and 22 cm.
sourceNotes: The peasant thumb (also called the afterthought or side-opening thumb) appears in Weldon's Practical Knitter from the 1880s and in Mary Thomas's Knitting Book (1938) as the standard low-complexity thumb for mittens. Both sources are out of UK and EU copyright.

glossaryTerms.definition: A thumb opening made by knitting a few stitches with waste yarn at the side of the hand, then continuing with the working yarn. After the hand is complete, the waste yarn is removed and the live stitches are picked up to work the thumb. Produces a side-of-palm thumb opening.
A method for knitting small circumferences in the round on one long circular needle. The cable is pulled into a loop at the midpoint so each half of the stitches sits on its own needle tip.

content.text: Full mittens in DK wool with a
peasant thumb
, worked in the round. Sized for hand circumferences of 18, 20, and 22 cm.

The peasant thumb is the most direct thumb method: one row of contrasting waste yarn marks where the thumb will sit. After the mitten hand is complete, the waste yarn is removed to expose live stitches above and below the gap. Those stitches become the thumb tube. There is no gusset and no shaping during the hand. The construction uses
magic loop
on a long circular. Budget about 95 g (210 m / 230 yards) of DK wool per pair.
What you need

items.name: Yarn
items.qty: 95 g (about 210 m / 230 yards) of DK-weight wool

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 3.75 mm (UK 9 / US 5) circular needle, at least 80 cm cable, for magic loop

items.name: Stitch markers
items.qty: 2: 1 for beginning of round, 1 for top shaping midpoint

items.name: Waste yarn
items.qty: About 30 cm of smooth contrasting yarn for the peasant thumb

content.text: Gauge
22 stitches and 28 rounds to 10 cm in stocking stitch on 3.75 mm needles.
Stitches used
Pattern
Before you cast on, circle your size. Every stitch count reads S (M, L) for hand circumferences 18 (20, 22) cm.
Cast on and cuff
Using the long-tail cast-on, cast on 40 (44, 48) stitches. Join to work in the round. Work 26 (28, 30) rounds of 2x2 rib. The cuff measures about 8.5 (9, 10) cm.
Hand body
Switch to stocking stitch. Work 8 (10, 10) rounds.
Thumb row
Using waste yarn, knit the first 10 (11, 12) stitches. Slip these stitches back to the left needle and knit them again with the working yarn. Continue in stocking stitch to end of round.
Hand above thumb
Continue in stocking stitch for 22 (24, 26) more rounds.
Top shaping

Place a marker at the midpoint. Decrease round: k1, ssk, knit to 3 before midpoint, k2tog, k1, SM, k1, ssk, knit to last 3, k2tog, k1. Plain round. Repeat until 8 stitches remain. Cut yarn and draw through all 8 stitches. Pull tight to close.
Thumb

Remove the waste yarn. Pick up 10 (11, 12) stitches from above the gap and 10 (11, 12) stitches from below. Total: 20 (22, 24) thumb stitches. Work 16 (18, 18) rounds of stocking stitch. Work 4 rounds of 1x1 rib. Bind off in rib.
Common faults

Hole at the corner of the thumb opening: one stitch was not picked up from the corner. Use the tapestry needle to pick up one strand from each corner gap stitch and work it as an extra stitch, then decrease it away on the next thumb round.
Waste yarn difficult to remove: the waste yarn was not smooth or was fuzzy. Use a very smooth waste yarn with no grip, such as a cotton or nylon cord.
Finishing
Weave in all tails on the wrong side.
Care
Hand wash in cool water. Lay flat to dry.
What to try next
The gusseted thumb gives a more anatomically correct fit at the base of the thumb. The gusseted thumb fingerless mitts pattern introduces the M1 increase needed to build the gusset.
